chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Yahya ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) divorced fifty women. Then Ali (peace be upon him) stood in al-Kufah and said: 'O people of al-Kufah! Do not give your women in marriage to al-Hasan, for he is a man who divorces frequently.'

Then a man stood up toward him and said: 'On the contrary, by God, we will surely give him in marriage, for he is the son of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) and the son of Fatimah (peace be upon her). If she pleases him, he keeps her; if he dislikes her, he divorces.'

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: To keep/retain — here used for retaining a wife in marriage
key_terms.مِطْلَاقٌ: One who divorces frequently; an intensive form indicating habitual divorce

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Hasan divorce fifty women according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam al-Hasan (AS) had divorced fifty women. When Imam Ali (AS) warned the people of al-Kufah not to give their daughters in marriage to al-Hasan, a man rebutted this advice, arguing that al-Hasan's noble lineage as the grandson of the Prophet (SAWW) and son of Fatimah (AS) justified his right to keep or divorce wives as he saw fit. This narrative reflects the early community's grappling with tensions between practical marital concerns and reverence for the Imams' sacred lineage.
word_analysis: we will indeed give him in marriage
